texts.preamble: Da vs Ashok Mangla Etc. on 10 May, 2018 In The Court Of Samar Vishal, Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate - Ii Patiala House Courts, New Delhi Cc No. 41270/2016 Date of Institution : 18.09.2007 Date of reserving judgement : 04.05.2018 Date of pronouncement : 10.05.2018 In re: Delhi Administration / Food Inspector Department of Pfa, Govt. of Nct of Delhi A-20, Lawrence Road Industrial Area, Delhi-110035 ... Complainant versus A1) Sh. Ashok Mangla S/o Late Sh B.R. Mangla, Shiva General Store Shop No. 1, Near Udasin Mandir, Aram Bagh, Paharganj, New Delhi -110055 R/o E-7, Aram Bagh, Chitra Gupta Rad, New Delhi 110055 A2) Sh Kishore Gambhir M/s Pee Gee Trading Co. 11055/2, East Park Road, Karol Bagh, New Delhi - 5 A3) Sh Vidyadhar Singh Manager Bhole Baba Milk Food Industries Ltd., 109 K.M. Stone Delhi Agra Road Dautana, Chhata District Mathura U.P. Cc No. 41270/2016 Page No. 1/11 Da vs Ashok Mangla etc. A4) Bhole Baba Milk Food Industries Ltd., 109 K.M. Stone Delhi Agra Road Dautana, Chhata District Mathura U.P. ... Accused person. Judgment: Da vs Ashok Mangla Etc. on 10 May, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136756705/ 1 1. The present is a complaint filed under section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954
texts.facts: The present is a complaint filed under section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (herein after referred to as PFA Act), alleging that the accused persons have violated the provisions of the PFA Act and Rules. 2. As per the complaint, on 18.04.2007, the Food Inspector (herein after referred to as FI) Shri M.K. Gupta and Field Assistant (herein after referred as FA) Shri Rajpal Singh under the supervision of Local Health Authority (herein after referred to as LHA)/SDM) Shri A.K. Verma visited the premises of Shiva General Store Shop No. 1, near Udasin Mandir, Aram Bagh, Paharganj, New Delhi 110055, where accused No. 1 Ashok Mangla was found conducting the business of food articles stored there, including "Ghee" for sale for human consumption, bearing identical label declaration. The sample consisted of three sealed plastic jars of 500 ml each of 'Ghee' taken as such bearing identical label declaration. The sample was taken under the supervision / direction of Sh. A.K. Verma, SDM/LHA. The Food Inspector divided the sample then and there into three equal parts. Each sample counter part containing the sample was separately packed, fastened and sealed according to PFA Act and Rules. The vendor's signatures were obtained on the LHA slip and the wrapper of DA vs Ashok Mangla etc. the sample counter parts. Notice in Form VI was given to accused No.1 Ashok Mangla and the price of sample was also given to him vide vendor receipt dated 18.04.2007. Panchnama too was prepared at the spot. All the documents prepared by F.I. were signed by accused No.1 Ashok Mangla and the other witness Sh. Raj Pal Singh, FA. Before starting sample proceeding efforts were made to join public witnesses but none came forward, as such Sh. Raj Pal Singh, FA was joined as witness. 3. One counter-part of the sample bearing LHA code No. 13/LHA/18312 was also sent to Public Analyst, Delhi in intact condition and remaining two counter-parts were deposited with the LHA in intact condition. Public Analyst analysed the sample. The report of the Public Analyst is as follows: "The sample does not conform to standard because B.R. exceeds the prescribed minimum limit of 43 and Reichert value is less than the prescribed minimum limit of 28" 4. It is the case of the complainant that accused No. 1 Ashok Mangla was the vendor-cum-proprietor of Shiva General Store Shop No. 1, Near Udasin Mandir, Aram Bagh, Paharganj, New Delhi 110055 at the time of sampling and he is in charge of and responsible for day to day conduct of the business of the shop. It is further stated that the sampled commodity was supplied to the accused No. 1 Ashok Mangla by M/s Pee Gee Trading Co. 11055/2, East Park Road, New Delhi - 5 vide bill No. 2330 Book No. 24 dated 15.03.2007. Accused no. 2 Kishore Gambhir confirmed the sale of the Ghee to Shiva DA vs Ashok Mangla etc. General Store and informed that the ghee was supplied to him by Bhole Baba Milk Food Industries Ltd., 109 K.M. Stone Agra- Delhi Road NH-2, Dautana, Chhata District Mathura U.P. Vide cash memo No. 1136 dated 14.03.2007. Accused No.4 Bhole Baba Milk Food Industries Ltd the manufacturer of ghee, had appointed accused No. 3 Vidyadhar Singh, Manager as nominee of the company under PFA Act and as such he is in charge and responsible for day to day conduct of the business of the company. Accused No. 4 Bhole Baba Milk Food Industries Ltd being manufacturing company is also liable. Accused No. 4 Bhole Baba Milk Food Industries Ltd had conformed the sale of the ghee to Pee Gee Trading Co. Da vs Ashok Mangla Etc. on 10 May, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136756705/ 2 5. Thereafter on completion of investigation, sanction under section 20 of the PFA Act was obtained from the Director PFA. The complaint was then filed in the court on 18.09.2007 alleging violation of section 2(ia)(a)(m) of PFA Act, 1954 as punishable section 7/16(1)(a) of PFA Act against the accused persons. 6. As the complaint was filed in writing by a public servant, recording of pre-summoning evidence was dispensed with and the accused was summoned vide order dated 18.09.2007. The accused thereafter exercised their option of analysing the counter part through CFL under section 13 (2) of the PFA Act. Based on the report of the CFL notice was framed against the accused for commission of the offence punishable under section 7/16(1) (a) PFA Act being violation of Section 2(ia) (a)&(m) of PFA Act, 1954 to which accused person pleaded DA vs Ashok Mangla etc. not guilty and claimed trial. 7. At the trial, the prosecution examined two witness in support of its case i.e. PW-1 FI Sh M.K. Gupta and PW-2 FA Sh Rajpal Singh. PW-1 and PW-2 were part of the team that had visited the spot for sample proceedings under the supervision of SDM/LHA Sh A.K Verma. These witness narrated the steps undertaken by them during the sample proceedings, including disclosing their identity, expressing intention to purchase sample for analysis, lifting the three plastic jars of of Ghee sealed 500 ml each, bearing identical label declaration, dividing the sample commodity into three equal parts by putting one originally sealed plastic jar of Ghee as one counterpart, separately sealing, packing and marking the same and obtaining signatures of vendor and witnesses. They also proved the necessary documents including the vendor's receipt Ex. PW-1/A, Notice in Form VI Ex.PW-1/B, Panchnama Ex.PW-1/C. A notice u/s 14 A Ex. PW 1/D was prepared at the spot addressing to the supplier as disclosed by the vendor at the spot. The accused furnished his statement Ex. PW 1/E at the spot alongwith photocopy of Bill of Purchase Ex. P1 and photocopy of his Voter I-Card Ex. P2. The accused also declaration in Form VI- B Ex. PW 1/F. Raid Report Ex. PW 1/G under Rule 9(e) was prepared at the s pot. Thereafter, on the next working day i.e. 19.04.2007, one counterpart alongwith a copy of Memo in Form VII in a sealed packet and another copy of Memo in Form VII in a separate sealed cover were deposited with PA vide PA's Receipt Ex. PW 1/H and the remaining two counterparts alongwith two copies of Memo in DA vs Ashok Mangla etc. Form VII in a sealed packet were deposited with LHA on 19.04.2007 vide LHA Receipt Ex. PW 1/I under intimation that one counterpart of the sample has already been deposited with the PA. Thereafter, PA Report Ex. PW 1/J was received through LHA according to which the sample was not conforming to the standards. Accordingly on the directions of SDM / LHA, PW-1 FI M.K. Gupta started the investigations. During investigation, PW-1 FI M.K. Gupta sent a letter Ex.PW1/K to VATO, Ward No. 4 and received its reply at portion X to X stating that no such firm in the name of M/s Shiva General Store was registered in that Ward. PW-1 FI M.K. Gupta also sent letter Ex. PW 1/K1 to VATO Ward No. 34 and received its reply stating that M/s PEE GEE Trading Company was registered as a proprietorship firm, having accused Kishore Gambhir as its Proprietor. Ex. PW 1/K1 sent a letter Ex. PW 1/K2 to M/s PEE GEE Trading Company and received its reply Ex. PW 1/K3 wherein they admitted the sale of purchase of the sample commodity to M/s Shiva General Store. Alongwith this reply they also provided photocopy of Bill of Purchase which is Ex. P3. Thereafter Ex. PW 1/K1 sent letter Ex. PW 1/L to M/s Bhola Baba Milk Food Industries Ltd. and received reply Ex. PW 1/L1 alongwith Da vs Ashok Mangla Etc. on 10 May, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136756705/ 3 documents Ex. P4, Ex.P5 & Ex.P6. He also received one more reply Ex. PW 1/L2 wherein it was disclosed that accused Vidhyadhar Singh was their Nominee. Thereafter on conclusions of investigations, PW-1 put the entire case file before the concerned SDM / LHA, who forwarded the same to the then Director PFA for obtaining his Consent and the then Director PFA Sh. N. Balachandran granted his Consent for prosecution of accused persons after DA vs Ashok Mangla etc. applying his mind vide Ex. PW 1/ M. Then the complaint Ex. PW 1/N before this Court and intimation letters Ex. PW 1/O alongwith copies of PA's Reports were sent to the accused persons through registered post Ex. PW 1/P, which were not received back undelivered. The witnesses were duly cross examined by the Ld Defence Counsel. 8. During trial the accused no. 1and 2 were discharged and the trial has proceeded against accused no. 3 and 4. Statement of the accused under section 313 CrPC were recorded on 21.03.2016 wherein the accused denied the allegations and pleaded innocence. Thereafter the matter was listed for defence evidence. 9. In their defence evidence, the accused examined one Dr. O.P. Singhal. Thereafter, vide order dated 20.11.2017 defence evidence was closed and the matter was listed for final arguments. 10. The commodity in the present case is 'Ghee', which apparently falls under item A.11.02.15 of Appendix B of Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955. It a standardized article under this Rule. There is no dispute about this fact even from the side of the accused, in as much as he never claimed that the food article was something else or other than ghee as governed by the said rule. The RM Value was 27.58 which shall not less than 28.0. As per CFL report, the BR reading was 44.5 and RM value was 26. According to both the reports, the sample was not confirming to standards as far as BR reading and RM Value of the Ghee is concerned. Therefore, the sample was tested by two experts, the report of both of them is almost same regarding adulteration.
texts.arguments: Defence Counsel has pointed out that the reports are at variance. It is pointed out that as per PA report, the BR reading was 43.9 but as per CFL report, it was 44.5. Again, according to PA report, RM value was 27.58 and as per CFL report it is 25.18. On this basis, the defence is seeking to claim that the samples were not representative due to said 'variations of more than 0.3%' in PA and CFL report. 13. In this regard, the defence strongly relies upon the judgement titled as Kanshi Nath v. State [2005(2) FAC 219], informing that the said ruling has been constantly followed by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in State v. Ramesh Chand [2010 (2) JCC 1250], Food Inspector v. Suresh Kumar [2010(2) FAC 204], K. D. Yadav v. State [2012(2) FAC 523] and Food Inspector v. Amar Chand [2016(1) FAC 190]. 14.This issue of variation was considered by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Delhi Administration vs Vidya Gupta Criminal Appeal No. 625 of 2018 dated 24.04.2018 wherein it was held that the finding of Hon'ble High Court in Kanshi Nath vs State and State vs Mahender Kumar & Ors, which hold that if in the comparison of reports of PA and the Director vast variations are found, then the samples are not representative, is improper.
